findings.title: Cleanup service ticker interval unintentionally reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: In `CleanUpService.Run`, the cleanup ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1` (while `clean` still uses a 9-minute timeout assuming a 10-minute period). This appears to be leftover local debugging code and will cause all background cleanup jobs (temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) to run 10x more frequently in production.

findings.title: Leftover Error-level debug logs in cleanup loop will spam logs with full ID slices
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` call `r.log.Error` before and after every batch deletion (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579), even when no error occurred and when `len(ids) == 0`. In addition to logging normal operation at `Error` level on every cleanup run, these calls log the entire `ids` slice, which can contain thousands of IDs per batch.

findings.title: Quadratic string concatenation when building SQLite DELETE IN clause
findings.body: In `deleteByIDs`, when building the `IN` list for SQLite with `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize > 999`, `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` is executed in a loop over `ids`. Because strings in Go are immutable, this copies the entire accumulated string on every iteration (O(N^2) time and allocations); for a batch of 32,767 IDs, a single call allocates hundreds of megabytes of transient strings. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt`) instead.
